title: ProjectE first-article (as-built) acceptance report
description: Output of tools/scripts/production/first_article.py. The gate is not 'were the files produced?' but 'does the board that was actually BUILT conform to the released package?' - the question cpl-assembly's own 'cannot prove' table hands off and nothing used to answer. Only gate.verdict == GREEN opens serial production.

evidence.description: The FAI evidence document this report read, with its digest. sha256 is null when the report was produced in-process rather than from a file - loud, not absent: a report that cannot be tied to its input is SCREEN_ONLY however good its contents.

package_binding.$comment: REVISION_MISMATCH -> STALE: good evidence about a different board. HASH_MISMATCH -> RED: same declared revision, different bytes, i.e. a silent substitution. UNBOUND -> CONFIRM: the assembler never said what it built from, and that was NOT assumed to match.

verdict.$comment: A subset of the closed vocabulary in skills/_shared/coverage-gate.md. NO new verdict is introduced. All five non-GREEN values block serial release equally; the precedence order (STALE > NO_COVERAGE > RED > CONFIRM > SCREEN_ONLY) is copied from gate_receipt.effective_status and only decides which reason is named first.

verdict_reasons.$comment: Empty only for GREEN. Reasons for the verdicts that also applied are prefixed [VERDICT], so a reader never has to re-run the gate to find the second blocker.

serial_release.$comment: true if and only if verdict == GREEN. This is the whole authority of this skill: open or hold the serial build.

release_meaning.$comment: 'Release' is ambiguous across the flow - Gerber release, accepted-first-article release, product release. This field pins which one this report is talking about, so a downstream reader cannot borrow the word for a claim this gate never made.

closed_by.$comment: This tool writes an acceptance receipt; it never validates it. A tool that grades its own receipt is marking its own homework.

coverage_by_class.description: Per-class coverage triples for the two populations with their own denominators: the hidden-joint (X-ray) universe and the moisture-sensitive (MSL) universe. Both are derived from the RELEASED PACKAGE, never from the evidence - evidence must not be allowed to shrink its own denominator.

explicitly_excluded.description: Refdes deliberately taken out of first-article scope by a named decision, each with a reason.

unaccounted_folded_into_excluded.description: Eligible refdes with NEITHER an inspection record NOR an exclusion. They are folded into coverage.excluded so scanned + excluded == eligible closes, and each one is ALSO raised as an UNACCOUNTED_REFDES violation in as_built_presence. The fold keeps the arithmetic honest; the simultaneous violation stops the fold from reading as a decision. Never one without the other.

class_unrecorded.description: The same fold, per class: hidden-joint refdes with no X-ray verdict and moisture-sensitive refdes with no handling record, each with the reason it was folded into that class's `excluded` count. Present so the per-class coverage triples are not the one place in the report where an exclusion has no stated reason.

excluded_checks.description: Whole checks taken out of the NO_COVERAGE rollup, with the reason. Only ever an EMPTY POPULATION declared by the released package (no hidden-joint part, no MSL>1 part, unpanelised build, no deviation raised), or an operator's --declare-out-of-scope. An empty population is a fact about the design; zero records over a non-empty population is a gap, and a gap is never excluded here.

metrics.description: check name -> violation count, or null when the check measured nothing. Null and not 0, for the reason board_check_report gives: a numeric 0 on an unmeasured check compares equal to a threshold and reports PASS on a check that examined nothing.

by_check.description: check name -> {status, scanned, violations}. Carries the coverage that `metrics` cannot. `by_check.<name>.status equals PASS` means ran + examined something + clean, because Finding refuses to build a scanned==0 PASS.

blockers.description: Every violation of every FAILed check, in gate-receipt/v1 blocker shape. GREEN is impossible while this list is non-empty - gate_receipt.validate_blockers enforces that independently.

feedback_edges.description: Which upstream owner the L2 feedback belongs to, by issue class. This gate classifies and routes; it never edits the upstream artefact.

parent_receipts.description: Hash-bound receipts this acceptance rests on, quoted from the evidence document.

declared_out_of_scope.$comment: The reason an operator gave for declaring the first-article gate out of scope. Setting it forces NO_COVERAGE; there is no flag that makes an unrun gate GREEN.

coverage.$comment: scanned + excluded == eligible, scanned <= eligible, violations <= scanned. The rule is enforced in code by common.findings.coverage_rule_violations; first_article refuses to emit a block that breaks it. `violations` counts SCANNED refdes only - an unaccounted refdes is a blocker, not a violation of something that was measured.

$comment: HARD RULE, enforced by the tool's design and by test_first_article.py: nothing here is derived from an image. Every acceptance is a structured decision made by a machine (AOI/X-ray) or a named human, carried with a hash-bound locator for the artefact behind it. The tool never opens the locator. An interpretive PHOTO/MANUAL record with no signoff_standard yields SCREEN_ONLY - somebody looked, nobody said what 'good' was - and SCREEN_ONLY does not open serial production. GREEN here is an as-built CONFORMANCE statement and not a reliability qualification: solder metallurgy and long-term joint life cannot be derived from one first article.
